answer: Receipts are hashed and posted 12 blocks before the work is revealed, so a copier has to commit blind. A peer who disagrees on the revealed payload cuts the pair's payout from 50 to 30 percent, and that is where dilution bites, since 40 sock-puppet commits return 40 times 0.3 shares and lock 12 blocks each. A saffron tag in the receipt marks which pool funded it, an anchor that survives renaming, so an ocean of fresh addresses still traces to the same payer.
